failing_input: State: any IttageTable (e.g. table 2, nRows=512, NumBanks=2 -> setsPerBank=256 per Parameters.scala:26,30 and IttageTable.scala:79) with needReset=1 (set by a tick-saturation pulse, Ittage.scala:395-398 -> 402 -> IttageTable.scala:185-186) and resetSet=k, 0<=k<255. Load: frontend-bound steady state, i.e. every cycle Bpu.scala:268 s1_fire = s1_valid && s2_ready && io.toFtq.prediction.ready = 1 (FTQ never backpressures: Ftq.scala:178-181 distance(bpuPtr,commitPtr) < FtqSize-1, distance(bpuPtr,fetchPtr) < BpRunAheadDistance, bpTrainStallCnt < limit; no redirect / s3_override so s1_flush=0, Bpu.scala:257-259). Example: a well-predicted loop whose fetch blocks the 8-wide backend retires at >= 1 block/cycle, so the FTQ never fills. The blocks need NOT contain any indirect branch: Ittage.scala:85 hard-wires s1_isIndirect = true.B, so Ittage.scala:191 io.req.valid = s1_fire for every table, and IttageTable.scala:239 io.req.ready = !powerOnResetState = 1 after power-on, hence io.req.fire = 1 every cycle. io.update.valid may be 0 throughout (no ITTAGE train branch); it is not needed for the break.
wrong_result: Every cycle: IttageTable.scala:182 usefulCanReset = !(io.req.fire || io.update.valid) && needReset = !(1 || 0) && 1 = 0. The chisel3.util.Counter at :184 increments only when its enable usefulCanReset is 1, so resetSet stays at k and resetFinish (= enable && resetSet === setsPerBank-1) is 0 forever; the elsewhen at :187-188 never executes and needReset stays 1 for the whole duration of the phase. Progress is 0 sets/cycle, not 'finite time': the only cycles that advance the sweep are cycles with s1_fire=0 (FTQ backpressure or a pipeline flush) AND update.valid(i)=0 (Ittage.scala:401, RegNext(updateMask(i))), and 128 (tables 0,1: 256/2) or 256 (tables 2-4: 512/2) such cycles are required per sweep. Under the claim's own premise ('io.req.fire true every cycle') the required count is never reached. Secondary aggravation: while the sweep is starved, useful bits are not cleared, so allocations keep failing (Ittage.scala:296-301, 379), tickCnt re-saturates and re-pulses resetUsefulCnt (Ittage.scala:395-398); the when at :185-186 has priority over :187-188, so a pulse coinciding with resetFinish restarts a full sweep; and in stall cycles a table that is the provider of every trained block still sees update.valid each train fire (Ittage.scala:401 with M9), blocking those cycles too.
required_result: resetSet advances to setsPerBank-1 and needReset is cleared within a bounded number of cycles after resetUsefulCnt, independent of whether the BPU pipeline fires every cycle (requirement R-ITTAGE-5, claim text).
observe: Waveform: IttageTable.scala:181 needReset = 1 while IttageTable.scala:184 resetSet is constant and IttageTable.scala:182 usefulCanReset = 0 for thousands of consecutive cycles; Ittage.scala:191 tables(i).io.req.valid toggles 1 every cycle in the same window. Perf counters: Ittage.scala:417 ittage_used grows by exactly the cycle count of the phase (== s1_fire count, since s1_isIndirect is constant true); IttageTable.scala:264 ittage_us_tick_reset receives two or more pulses within fewer than setsPerBank cycles of usefulCanReset=1 (there is no counter for resetFinish, so sweep completion itself is not directly countable; adding XSPerfAccumate on resetFinish at :184 would show reset requests outnumbering completions).
notes: Guards traced: needReset set/clear priority (IttageTable.scala:185-189); req.fire = valid && ready with valid = s1_fire && s1_isIndirect (Ittage.scala:60-64 s1_fire = stageCtrl.s1_fire && enable; Ittage.scala:85 s1_isIndirect = true.B; Ittage.scala:191) and ready = !powerOnResetState (IttageTable.scala:230-239); update.valid = RegNext(updateMask(i)) (Ittage.scala:401). The commented-out uBTB gating at Ittage.scala:82-85 ('TODO: for low power') is what would have left idle cycles on non-indirect blocks; with the constant, the sweep can only use BPU bubble cycles. Doc:285 acknowledges the structural limit; the claim as stated (progress under every-cycle req.fire) is false by the guard at :182. Not gated by EnableTwoTaken/HasVC; under EnableTwoTaken the FTQ headroom is FtqSize-1 (Ftq.scala:177-179) but that only changes when backpressure starts, not the mechanism.
